condition: Drawn swan permit only, in Churchill, Lyon and Pershing counties. All swan hunting closes once 10 trumpeter swans are taken; check whether the quota has been reached.
evidence: NDOW 2026-27 guide: swans may be hunted 'provided the trumpeter swan quota has not been reached'; 'If a total harvest of ten (10) trumpeter swans is reached, the swan season is closed.' 50 CFR 20.107 (2025-26): 'Harvests of trumpeter swans are limited to 20 in Utah and 10 in Nevada.'
source_titles: NDOW 2026-2027 Small Game Hunting Regulations|50 CFR 20.107 swan seasons (Migratory Bird Hunting; 2025-26 Seasons)

evidence: Idaho's controlled swan hunt allows 1 swan with a bill-measurement check; neither IDFG's 2026-27 guide nor 50 CFR 20.107 gives Idaho a trumpeter quota or any species-specific trumpeter authorization. A generic swan season does not establish trumpeter take.
source_titles: Idaho Migratory Game Bird 2026-2027 Seasons & Rules|50 CFR 20.107 swan seasons (Migratory Bird Hunting; 2025-26 Seasons)

evidence: Alberta's unprotected 'blackbirds' names no member species; the audit's member list came from range, which a group season cannot establish.

South Dakota lists rusty blackbird among birds not protected or conditionally protected (SDCL 41-11-10): depredation and nuisance take only. Unprotected status alone does not admit a species (owner inclusion rule, 2026-09-30).
source_titles: SDCL 41-11-10 Birds not protected or conditionally protected

evidence: Alaska's small game regulations name a resident season, but pelagic cormorant is protected under the Migratory Bird Treaty Act and has no federal hunting framework in 50 CFR 20; the federal basis for the state season is unresolved.
source_titles: 2026-2027 Alaska Hunting Regulations: Fur Animals and Small Game

evidence: Connecticut's cottontail season does not distinguish New England from eastern cottontail; a generic group season does not establish take of this species.
Vermont's hare and rabbit season names cottontail rabbits without distinguishing New England cottontail.

Alaska lists Feral Ferret among 'Deleterious exotic wildlife' with no limit and no closed season, beside rats, mice, pigeons and English sparrows: a removal listing for any unconfined domestic ferret, not a hunting opportunity. The domestic ferret has no established free-ranging population in North America: state agency surveys found no breeding feral populations (CDFW, California Fish and Wildlife Journal 2022), and GBIF holds 4 US and 0 Canadian records 1990-2026, all of zoo or captive animals.
source_titles: 2026-2027 Alaska Hunting Regulations: Fur Animals, Small Game, Unclassified Game|Impacts of domesticated ferrets upon wildlife, agriculture, and human health in the USA (California Fish and Wildlife Journal, 2022)
